subject: Re: POC planning — trial access, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finapps.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC planning — Redwood trial access & success criteria

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned. Great conversation and it sounds like a 2-week POC will help validate latency/cost signals and basic integration flows.

Agreed success criteria (what FinApps will evaluate):
- 95th percentile infer latency < 250ms for gen endpoints under 5 concurrent sessions
- Token cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your target cost baseline
- Embedding similarity quality on your fraud-detection prompt set (A/B to existing embeddings)
- No PII leakage on sample traffic and observability into prompt-level logs

POC plan and timeline:
- Week 1 (Mar 8–Mar 12): Provisioning + integration (API keys, IP allowlist, SSO invite). Basic smoke tests and sample prompts.
- Week 2 (Mar 15–Mar 19): Load/latency tests, embedding experiments, and quality evals.
- Wrap & decision: Mar 22 — review results, discuss next steps (Dedicated vs hosted).

Ownership / who does what:
- Redwood: Dev Patel (provision keys, create scoped POC key, help with IP allowlist and SSO invites), Michael Grant (runtime monitoring & perf checks)
- FinApps: Alex (product lead, coordinates test users), Priya (security/IT will provide SAML metadata and IP ranges), Luke (engineering contact)

Access needs from FinApps to provision:
- List of tester emails for SSO invites (or a SAML metadata file)
- IP ranges to add to our allowlist for API key binding
- Preference on API key type: scoped POC key (token-based) or service account?

Attachments: FinApps_POC_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW / goals & timelines).

Next steps (action items):
1) Alex/Priya: confirm tester list + IP ranges by EOD Wed Mar 4
2) Dev: provision scoped POC API key and send instructions once we have IPs/SAML
3) Michael: pre-config runtime monitors & cost dashboards

If that looks right I’ll spin up the SOW for signature and get credentials ready once we have the inputs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finapps.com>, Luke Brennan <luke.brennan@finapps.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:35:12 -0500
Subject: Re: POC planning — Redwood trial access & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks good. Quick answers from our side:
- Test users: alex.johnson@finapps.com, luke.brennan@finapps.com, qa+llm@finapps.com
- IP ranges to allowlist: 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24 (we’ll confirm if our egress changes by Friday)
- For the POC we prefer a scoped API key rather than a long-lived service account key; rotation policy should be documented

Priya, I’ve looped you for SAML metadata — our IT team can provide metadata.xml and add redwood.ai as a relying party.

Also: can Redwood generate the scoped key and tie it to the allowlisted IPs, or should we create one from the console? Either way works — we just need the rotation guidance.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Product Lead, FinApps
alex.johnson@finapps.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700

On Tue, Mar 3, 2026 at 09:35 AM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — that summary looks good. Quick answers from our side:
> - Test users: alex.johnson@finapps.com, luke.brennan@finapps.com, qa+llm@finapps.com
> - IP ranges to allowlist: 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24

Thanks Alex — we can definitely do that. Short answers / plan from my side: 
- I’ll generate a scoped POC API key and bind it to the IP ranges you provided. We will send the key to the listed test users via the secure instructions below (do not post keys in Slack/email).
- If you provide SAML metadata.xml, we’ll issue SSO invites and can enable Just-In-Time user provisioning (if you want SCIM we can set that up later).
- Rotation: for POC we’ll set auto-expiry at 90 days, but I’ll include guidance to rotate every 14 days during the POC if you want extra security.

I’ve attached a short instructions file (redwood_poc_credentials_instructions.txt) with the steps we’ll take to provision and how to test:
- Generate scoped API key tied to allowlist
- Provide curl examples for gen & embeddings endpoints
- Show how to check request logs and token usage in Console

Planned timeline (when I’ll do the work):
- Wed Mar 4: receive final IP ranges + SAML metadata -> create scoped key & send instructions
- Thu Mar 5: SSO invites sent (pending metadata)
- Mon Mar 8: POC integration window begins

Action items assigned:
- Alex: confirm the IP ranges above and confirm whether testers want 14-day rotation or standard 90-day expiry
- Priya: share SAML metadata.xml and SSO admin contact (it-admin@finapps.com)
- Me (Dev): provision keys & publish instructions once we have the inputs
- Michael: will validate perf dashboards are ready before Mar 8

Thanks — I’ll wait on the metadata + final IPs and then proceed.

--
Dev Patel
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

(attachment: redwood_poc_credentials_instructions.txt - includes curl samples and step-by-step on allowlist binding)

Thanks everyone. We can provide the SAML metadata and confirm the IP ranges (34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24). Our SSO admin (it-admin@finapps.com) will send the metadata.xml by EOD today.

A couple of quick asks from security: 
- Please include instructions on how to rotate the scoped API key during the POC (Dev, noted you’ll include that).
- Can we get a short Data Processing Addendum or a pointer to your security docs (SOC2 report) ahead of the trial? That will help our compliance team sign off quickly.

Also: we would prefer Redwood to generate the scoped key and tie it to the allowlist — that reduces friction on our side.

Alex — happy to sign the SOW via DocuSign once Marissa sends it. Our legal will reference deal DBL-2026-0347.
